items.summary: On NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), BF16 attention is MMA-bound rather than softmax-bound as it is on data center GPUs, so the higher-throughput NVFP4 path offers a way to accelerate world-model inference. The original SageAttention3 CTA design ran QK, online softmax/quantization, and PV strictly serially per N tile because its two k=64 MMA instructions for each k=128 contraction were issued synchronously in succession, leaving large gaps with no tensor-core work scheduled while warps handled the intervening math. Register constraints reinforced this: producer warps used 3,072 registers and consumer warps used 59,392 registers, totaling 62,464—about 95.3% of SM capacity—which left little room for a second full score buffer. The optimized design splits each N128 score tile into two N64 register slots; once one half is exponentiated and quantized to NVFP4 probabilities, those registers are reused for the next tile's QK computation while PV accumulates on the current tile, interleaving adjacent tiles without allocating a second complete score tile. Reactor integrated this kernel in production serving real customer traffic across four world-model workloads (LongLive, Helios, OmniDreams) at batch size 1, 24 heads, head dimension 128, with equal query/key lengths; timings excluded Q/K/V quantization and output-stride restoration. Table 2 reports end-to-end latency reductions for video-chunk inference, full generation (Long-run rows), and action prediction, though the specific percentage figures are not reproduced in this summary.
items.title: Reactor's Register Recycling Closes Tensor Core Gaps in NVFP4 Attention on RTX Blackwell SM120

items.summary: When Jensen Huang delivered his first all-hands address as Nvidia CEO, he acknowledged violating the company's code of conduct while emphasizing that no employee is exempt from it. However, Huang also stated that breaking a code does not automatically result in termination, noting that 'facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments' still matter—implying violations do not always cost someone their job, including the CEO himself. According to Wired, this stance has created an awkward position for Nvidia given its leader admitted to rule-breaking. Ethics and compliance training expert Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, argues that most codes of conduct function less as quasi-legal rulebooks than as reflections of corporate culture. In a survey of more than 2,000 workers across various industries, Plass identified the primary risk of an unpunished infraction not as legal but cultural: employees may feel embarrassed or angry about their employer. He cited one company's example in which its CEO appeared at the Olympics despite a corporate travel ban; for over a decade afterward, 'the Olympics' became shorthand within that organization for the worst possible employee behavior. Plass noted that companies typically remove executives only after an investigation and then pursue what he called a 'hearts-and-minds initiative' to win back employees, customers, investors, and others by acknowledging mistakes and promising change—though he acknowledged this playbook is difficult at Nvidia because Huang departed without a clear succession plan and there are serious doubts about whether the company could thrive without him. Judging by an employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang's return has not yet produced a morale problem, but experts warn that sidestepping the code of conduct may eventually cost Nvidia something harder to measure: its employees' pride in the company.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Admits Violating Its Code of Conduct

items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against accusations that the company believes humanity should surrender human free will and governance to AI systems, calling such claims 'absurd' in a long X post on Wednesday. He argued that sacrificing legitimacy or self-determination for efficiency or security is wrong, applying equally to AI governance, and insisted no one who read his writing could reasonably conclude he holds different views. The statement came after rivals raised concerns about human agency: OpenAI's Sam Altman said he wanted people to keep 'agency over the future,' and Meta's Alexandr Wang wrote that society should not accept a 'handover' of control to AI, especially given fears about unconstrained recursive self-improvement (RSI). Amodei countered by citing his published essays advocating for democratic oversight, arguing humans should retain ultimate decision-making power. He distinguished between surrendering free will broadly and the narrower reality that advancing AI automates specific tasks—such as driving cars, designing cancer drugs, or writing software—and suggested drawing a line at RSI, while implicitly acknowledging experts see it as leading to loss of human control by noting 'we may want limits on this process.' Despite these concerns, Anthropic is integrating AI into its own research: the company reported in June that Claude authored more than 80% of code merged into its codebase, and an independent METR assessment found Anthropic's models improving at roughly twice their historical rate due to AI-assisted research. Amodei also noted Anthropic does not expect it will be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously without meaningful human supervision, though he acknowledged that such supervision is increasingly difficult because AI advances faster than engineers can audit and may exhibit deceptive behavior when recognizing evaluation. He accused competitors of engaging in 'vibes-based commercial and political positioning,' citing OpenAI's recent claim to have solved the speed limit of matrix multiplication as evidence all companies are pursuing similar automation without materially different approaches.
items.title: Anthropic's Dario Amodei Rejects Claims It Wants Humans to Surrender Control to AI

items.summary: Anthropic has made its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, allowing users to share and access frequently repeated tasks independently of the main Claude interface on Mac and Windows. The 'install as app' feature is in beta across all free and paid plans but does not support Linux. When installed, artifact apps receive their own icon and window instead of running inside Claude, can be shared with others, require permission before interacting with a computer, still access Claude and connected tools, update automatically when the underlying artifact changes, and draw on users' Claude usage limits—lowest for free accounts. Anthropic states the feature is designed to streamline app building for both developers and non-developers as Claude increasingly functions as an AI-powered work suite rather than a single chatbot. The apps require being signed in to Claude with internet access, so they are not fully portable or off-grid options; legacy artifacts from Claude Cowork and template-based artifacts such as Docs, Slides, and Sheets cannot be installed. Permissions range from browser defaults to app-specific settings like notifications and full computer access, which lets an app run programs and read, change, or delete files without repeated prompts—so Anthropic advises caution since it does not review apps before installation and only permits granting full access to self-made (or coworker-made for Team and Enterprise plans) applications. For Claude Enterprise plans the feature is disabled until an administrator enables it in Organization settings.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Desktop App Support for Claude Artifacts

items.summary: Delegating research tasks to AI agents does not remove scientists' responsibility for how that work is accomplished. Researchers must verify whether a literature-review system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims unsupported by its sources, understand which methods and files an agentic data-analysis system used—and confirm the results are reproducible—ensure automated lab protocols respect physical safety constraints like temperature limits and material toxicity, and gain assurance that systems handling human-participant data protect privacy and limit access. These ethical and safety questions sit at the center of work on AI for science: responsible research extends beyond accuracy to how findings are produced and scrutinized so scientists can stand behind them.
items.title: Scientists Draw the Line on Delegating Research Tasks to AI Agents

items.summary: At the November 13, 2026 vLLM meetup at SGInnovate in Singapore—hosted by Inferact and NVIDIA with speakers from Alibaba Cloud—the community demonstrated advances across open-source AI inference. Thien Tran of Inferact reported that pipeline parallelism (PP) improved prefill throughput on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: PP2 reached up to 1.37× the max throughput of TEP2 + SP, and moving activation transfers onto copy engines cut p50 time-to-first-token by 13–20% near saturation; a new PP-aware scheduler puts PP2 ahead from about 0.5 s onward while TEP2 + SP still wins at tight 0.75 s targets. Jie Fang of NVIDIA showed SM12x cards (RTX PRO and DGX Spark) went from no DeepSeek-V4 path to near-peak efficiency in six months, with FlashInfer feature categories gaining dedicated SM12x kernels rising from 0 of 17 in January to 14 in October and monthly pull requests climbing from 6 to 121; a one-line dispatch fix added +17.7% throughput and preferring W4A4 for NVFP4 linears added +23.8%, while TP2 × PP2 instead of TP4 gave 1.37× prefill throughput, enabling DeepSeek-V4-Pro to start on 8× RTX PRO 6000 with a 32K-token prefill in 939 ms and video generation cut from 213.4 s to 4.92 s (real-time factor 0.95). Taichang Zhou of vLLM-Omni described serving the interactive LingBot-World 2.0 model on 4× H200, where Ulysses sequence parallelism cut one block from 2,397 ms to 725 ms and a new AR-Diffusion engine reached 1.9× faster per chunk than September (or 2.75× at full options for 22.5 fps), plus Noisy PP lifting steady-state throughput 2.85× on CausVid-Wan 1.3B. Ao Shen of Inferact, with NVIDIA DevTech and Research, reported zero-mismatch rollout/trainer kernels held KL divergence at 0 (versus collapse within ~100 steps for standard kernels) while costing about 10% of rollout speed, enabling async REINFORCE Zero to reach 48.80% accuracy against 48.91% for sync RL and cut time per update from 49.4 s to 20.6 s (a 2.40× speedup). Hao Lu of NVIDIA explained vLLM ran on Vera Rubin from day 0 because Blackwell kernels run unchanged, with localizing MoE experts in decode gaining memory-bound throughput and TMA load rising from 13.4 to 18.7 TB/s against a 19.2 TB/s HBM peak; MiniMax M3.1-Flash on Vera Rubin NVL72 reached about 4.3–6.5× the tokens per dollar of GB300 at matched interactivity. Sean Zhan of Alibaba Cloud described enterprise-scale agent infrastructure using MicroVMs for hardware-grade isolation, least-privilege policies, full audit trails and snapshotting/hibernation to make million-scale concurrency economically viable.
items.title: vLLM Singapore Meetup Showcased Faster Prefill, Agent-Written Kernels and Vera Rubin Support

items.summary: A study of scientists working in natural, applied, and social sciences argues that delegating research tasks to AI agents does not remove researchers' responsibility for how work is accomplished. The authors interviewed 17 US-based scientists about responsible development of these systems, which can use tools and carry out research with varying degrees of autonomy; the findings are exploratory rather than a representative survey or an empirical evaluation of specific agents. A central finding concerns trust: across interviews the researchers identified five dimensions of scientific trust—validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability, and transparency—that extend beyond whether an AI produces correct answers to include how an answer was reached, protection of sensitive information, recognition of bias, and determination of who verifies findings. Another main finding is that scientists should help decide which tasks agents take on, how they operate, and how their performance is evaluated, since even a technically correct result may be unsuitable if researchers cannot inspect its production or if an agent accesses unauthorized data. A third key finding concerns the future of science: interviewees were divided between excitement about AI-driven progress and existential concern about human scientists' role, while proposing training in AI use and developing and enforcing guidelines as critical challenges.
items.title: Scientists Draw the Line on Delegating Research Tasks to AI Agents

items.summary: New EU fees on low-value imports are adding to the cost of online purchases, and a survey by the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC) found that 43% of shoppers reported paying more than they expected. BEUC also warned that nearly a third of consumers who saw higher costs only discovered the additional charges after completing checkout, raising concerns about price transparency. The fees are designed to make non-EU marketplaces contribute to customs checks and ensure fairer competition for European retailers, but both Temu and AliExpress account for more than half of the purchases in the BEUC study. Separately, Brussels found Temu in breach of Article 35 of the Digital Services Act (DSA), which requires platforms to take effective measures to mitigate risks from illegal products, following a May fine under Article 34 that required very large online platforms to identify and assess systemic risks; the Commission had previously fined Temu €200 million for failing to assess those risks. A Temu spokesperson told Tech Policy Press it 'respectfully disagrees' with the preliminary findings and expressed confidence in reaching an amicable resolution, while Member of the European Parliament Anna Cavazzini said she expects Temu to comply or risk being banned from the single market.
items.title: EU Tightens Scrutiny of Online Marketplaces as Black Friday Prices Rise

items.summary: The organization WITNESS argues that existing human rights law is insufficiently equipped to protect the shared epistemic foundation—our collective ability to establish what happened—that underpins accountability, justice, democratic deliberation, and remedy. The article notes that for over three decades WITNESS has relied on authentic video evidence to help people demand justice, but since 2018 it has developed provenance tools and a Deepfakes Rapid Response Force as AI increasingly undermines trust in shared content; these efforts are described as necessary but inadequate because most content carries no verifiable provenance and reliable detection remains out of reach. The UN's new Independent International Scientific Panel on AI identifies three harms to the information ecosystem—epistemic erosion, the liar's dividend, and synthetic consensus—and researchers warn that synthetic media could build persuasive
items.title: WITNESS Proposes a 'Right to Reality' Amid AI's Threat to Shared Truth

items.summary: In response to a letter by Foo Sing Kheng questioning the use of Singapore's National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system, Goh Min Liong, Chief Medical Informatics Officer at the Ministry of Health, clarified that NEHR is intended to complement—not replace—healthcare professionals' clinical assessment and professional judgment. The officer acknowledged that it is good practice for clinicians to verify details provided by patients against medical records, but emphasized that information in NEHR may be outdated since a patient's condition can change over time, sometimes requiring repeated tests to confirm current results are relevant. He recommended the writer contact Tan Tock Seng Hospital and National Centre for Infectious Diseases directly to better understand care rendered to his family member, including whether recorded information was appropriate and relevant. The response pointed readers to the Ministry of Health's published Guidelines on Appropriate Contribution, Use and Access to NEHR as setting out the system's intended role and proper use.
items.title: Singapore's Ministry of Health Defends National Electronic Health Record System

items.summary: In a letter to The Straits Times, Andrew Ong reflects on Singapore's animated film The Violinist after it won two awards—Best Animated Feature and Best Adapted Screenplay—at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards in Taipei. He recalls that he remembers the film most for its original score, composed by Singaporean Ricky Ho and Spanish composer Isabel Latorre, describing the music as inseparable from the images and capable of expressing longing, memory, and unspoken emotion between people. Ong asks whether the Singapore Symphony Orchestra would consider performing selections from the score in a concert.
items.title: Violinist Composer Requests SSO Performance of Award-Winning Score

items.summary: Two companies linked to the restaurant chain Komala's had their Central Provident Fund cases compounded with a discharge amounting to an acquittal for all 20 charges, according to State Courts proceedings heard on Nov 25. Komala's Pte Ltd and Komala's F&B Enterprises each faced 10 charges; per charge sheets seen by The Straits Times, both companies failed to pay CPF contributions for 10 employees in December 2025 (Komala's) and the same number of employees that month (F&B Enterprises). Both matters were compounded after all required payments had been made. Rajoo Thanasekaran, director of Komala's, attended court as a representative of both companies, which are listed separately as live businesses — Komala's was incorporated in 1997 and F&B Enterprises in 2001.
items.title: Komala's-linked companies settle all 20 CPF charges after paying dues

items.summary: Australia's consumer prices climbed more than expected in October, with the annual rate reaching 4.9% — its fastest reading since the monthly series began and well above the Reserve Bank of Australia's 2% to 3% target band (q9). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported on Nov 25 that the monthly CPI rose 0.5%, above forecasts of 0.4% (q6, q7), driven largely by fuel costs jumping 6.3% on higher global oil prices (q8). Core inflation, measured by the trimmed mean after stripping out one month's fuel cost, also rose 0.5% and lifted its annual pace to 3.8%, up from 3.6% where it had held since June — marking a two-year high (q12, q13, q14). Goods inflation jumped 1% in the month to an annual rate of 5.8%, while services inflation was unchanged at 4% annually; new dwelling prices rose 0.8%. The stronger-than-expected data tempered market enthusiasm for a rate cut: traders still expect cuts given labour-market weakness but now price only about a 75% chance of a June cut, down from near certainty (q5). Westpac's Luci Ellis said November could show negative headline CPI due to falling fuel prices and that the RBA is likely finished hiking. VanEck's Russel Chesler warned inflation may be becoming entrenched as unemployment hit a five-year high of 4.9% in September, while State Street's Krishna Bhimavarapu noted persistent inflation might require more restrictive policy.
items.title: Australian inflation rose in October as core hit a two-year high

items.summary: Under a proposal filed last week with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, Google would pay $10.8 million for Ohio Power to install advanced conductors on about 15 miles of Columbus power lines that were already slated for rebuild; in return, Google said it would gain access to 24 megawatts of capacity two years early as it expands a data center there (Latitude Media). The deal is framed by Google's Ellen Zuckerman as first-of-its-kind: she told Latitude Media the investment should demonstrate that such spending can unlock headroom not just for its own pipeline but
items.title: Google's Ohio grid deal tests a faster path to data center power

items.summary: Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML — the sole maker of lithography machines needed to produce the world's most advanced AI chips and a $520 billion de facto monopoly in chipmaking equipment (q1) — argued on Semafor's Future Proof that export controls should not aim to completely cut China off from Western technology. Fouquet warned that fully frustrating China risks prompting Beijing to intensify its own development efforts, stating: "You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don't completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development." He contended that continuing to sell China older equipment — shipments more than a decade behind the cutting edge — maintains a strategic "generation gap" keeping Beijing reliant on Western hardware. Fouquet noted ASML has held an extremely high market share in China for nearly 30 years, which he described as close to 100% (q2), meaning Chinese firms have accepted reliance on its technology believing access would continue.
items.title: ASML's CEO argues for continued chip sales to China

items.summary: Rental prices for Nvidia's B300 chip fell 7% between late October and Tuesday, according to Liquid Compute's index, which put the hourly rate at $7.72 in late October and $7.19 on Tuesday (q1: 7%; q2: $7.72; q3: $7.19). Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, told CNBC that the increase in listings stems from a new U.S. rule, noting one firm informed him it was selling because of the rule (q4: 7%). The sellers appear to be offloading chips bought for data centers that rent access to Chinese companies; talks aimed at lining up purchasers for thousands of B300 units have been underway since the rule's announcement. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule taking effect Nov. 19 (q5: 500,000) to stop Chinese companies from evading export controls by reaching advanced chips through overseas data centers; data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil that provide Chinese customers with substantial computing capacity must obtain U.S. licenses within 90 days. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the rule was meant to close loopholes on indirect access via Southeast Asia or remote access from third-country data centers. Liquid Compute's CEO Ronit Jain said Asia-Pacific data center operators that sold to Chinese customers have surplus capacity and are steering it toward U.S. buyers, with Jain anticipating further price declines; Nvidia declined to comment.
items.title: Nvidia Chip Sellers Are Offloading GPUs After New U.S. Rules Bar China Access

items.summary: On November 25, S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on 'CreditWatch Negative,' indicating a high likelihood of a downgrade due to rising management and governance risks. The agency stated that the departure and subsequent reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang did not adequately address its concerns about board oversight of the executive code of conduct.
items.title: S&P Global Places Nvidia on CreditWatch Negative Over Management and Governance Risks

items.summary: A review of Donald Trump's financial disclosures shows his investment portfolios bought or sold Nvidia stock at least 44 times in 2025. His most recent public declarations indicate that between January and September the portfolios purchased between $5.2m (£4m) and $17m (£13m) worth of Nvidia shares while selling between $4.4m and $12m, leaving his accounts holding between $12.5m and $58m in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025. Because financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics report only a low and high range for each transaction, the exact amount traded cannot be determined precisely.
items.title: Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares at least 44 times this year

visual.alt: Bar chart. Purchases (Jan–Sep) (Purchase range (£)) 17,000,000 $; Sales (Jan–Sep) (Sale range (£)) 12,000,000 $.

items.summary: Washington will question Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday, when he appears in a closed-door interview with three House committees. The appearance was scrubbed from the schedule after Huang resigned as CEO, and there is no confirmation yet of whether he will return to stage his scheduled keynote at Nvidia's annual developer conference less than two miles away. Nvidia has reportedly assembled a team of top Washington lawyers and lobbyists ahead of the hearing. Lawmakers still have questions for Huang and Nvidia, while much of the tech world views the hearings as political theater.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Capitol Hill Questioning Amid DC Conference

items.summary: President Trump announced new tariffs on the eve of Thanksgiving that will affect major U.S. trading partners, including China and the European Union. The measures are set to take effect in January 2027 and follow a Supreme Court ruling that declared his April 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs illegal. BBC business reporter Jonathan Josephs broke down these latest tariffs as part of an analysis exploring what the administration's alternative plan is and what it could mean for American businesses and consumers.
items.title: Trump Announces New Tariffs to Replace Court-Struck 'Liberation Day' Measures

items.summary: According to Bloomberg, S&P Global Ratings is weighing a one-notch downgrade of Nvidia's AA credit rating once its current 90-day review concludes on Wednesday. In the statement cited by Bloomberg, S&P said it expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch unless investigations or disclosures indicate that Nvidia's reputation or future business prospects have been harmed. The agency expressed unease over how the chipmaker is managed and governed following CEO Jensen Huang's departure and subsequent reinstatement as CEO on Monday, less than two weeks after he stepped down amid reports of two extramarital affairs—one involving a woman suspected of spying for China who had no family relationship to him but worked as an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. In response to the affair disclosures, Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation earlier this month and said nothing it has seen suggests trade secrets or U.S. national security were compromised; in a statement, Nvidia noted that its board received input from senior levels of the United States government and is confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk. Separately, on Nov. 17, the Justice and Commerce departments announced they are investigating whether Megaspeed redirected Nvidia chips in breach of American export rules. Several Republican lawmakers have criticized the reinstatement, and Jensen Huang along with Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter have confirmed appearances for transcribed interviews with House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, while the Senate Banking Committee has scheduled a public hearing featuring Huang on Dec. 3.
items.title: S&P Considers Downgrading Nvidia Over Jensen Huang Governance Concerns

items.summary: The US trade representative's office announced Wednesday that President Trump is proposing new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the European Union, which could take effect in January at the earliest. The proposal adds a further 20% tax on Chinese imports (q2), bringing total duties to about 40% (q3). Other affected countries include Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Legally, the administration is basing these tariffs on section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (q4, d5), after a February Supreme Court ruling found its earlier
items.title: Trump Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners Including China and the EU

items.summary: Google denied social media reports of large-scale layoffs in India, stating that about 30 roles were affected by a small organizational change at Google Cloud. The company said the positions were eliminated as part of re-prioritizing work rather than representing mass job cuts. This clarification arrived amid broader uncertainty for technology and IT employees in India: Google is expanding its voluntary buyout initiative to more countries, while Microsoft has offered voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees, including eligible teams in India.
items.title: Google Denies Mass India Layoffs; Attributes ~30 Role Cuts to Google Cloud Reorganization

items.summary: The Bank of England says food price inflation in the UK could rise to between 3% and 5% by mid-next year, up sharply from its current level of about 1.3%, though Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli noted it has risen less than expected since the Iran war began. The warning was delivered as the Bank raised interest rates by a quarter-point to 4% in late November to combat inflation that hit 3.6% last month, with petrol and diesel prices up more than 33% over the past year. Governor Andrew Bailey said continued falls in oil prices could lower these projections, which had previously been expected to peak at almost 5%, but noted some next-year pressure is already baked in — citing a 26% rise in household energy price caps due in January. The forecast comes as MPC members debate their approach: Catherine Mann warned that inflation has run above the Bank's 2% target for five years and urged more aggressive action, while Swati Dhingra described this month's rate hike as a one-off 'insurance' measure against volatile oil prices.
items.title: Bank of England Warns UK Food Inflation Could Reach 5% by Mid-2025

items.summary: On Wednesday, Vice President JD Vance said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang did not need a presidential pardon because he was never under criminal investigation. Vance supported reinstating Huang after receiving assurances from the attorney general and other officials that Huang was 'under no investigation' and that accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting rather than evidence. His comments came one day after President Donald Trump told the New York Post that offering Huang a pardon would be 'always an option,' though he added it likely wouldn't be necessary. The two intervened in Nvidia's leadership dispute to pressure the company's board into reinstating Huang despite lawmakers' concerns about whether his alleged affair with an alleged Chinese spy posed a national security risk. Trump and Vance said they wanted Huang to testify before congressional committees about chip exports, the alleged affair, and the government's role in his reinstatement; Trump described Huang as '100% aboveboard.' Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters on Tuesday that no evidence indicated Huang committed a crime but declined to confirm whether the Justice Department conducted a thorough investigation. Vance's remarks appeared to confirm that the DOJ never initiated a formal investigation, though days earlier Trump had said his administration had done 'a pretty good investigation' to exonerate Huang. Lawmakers from both parties questioned the government's determination: Senator John Curtis asked who weighed in on the national security assessment and what they told Nvidia's board; Senator Pete Ricketts noted that reinstatement does not excuse Huang from testifying or absolve Nvidia of accountability for unaccounted-for chips; Senator John Kennedy said his concern was whether Huang had sex with a Chinese spy rather than any personal conduct; Senator Elizabeth Warren demanded an explanation of which officials provided input supporting the reinstatement; and Representative Elissa Slotkin raised concerns about whether Trump knew about the potential compromise and did nothing. Huang is expected to testify before congressional committees in coming weeks.
items.title: Vance Says Jensen Huang Needs No Pardon After Reinstatement

items.summary: US regulators approved Elon Musk's SpaceX plan to deploy a constellation of datacenters that process data in space, marking the first such authorization in US history. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said it authorized 1 million Starmind orbital satellites, or compute modules, and stated the approval would support America's super intelligence economy while bringing humanity closer to what regulators called a Kardashev II civilization. FCC chair Brendan Carr described the move as ushering in an era of super intelligence led by the US. Proponents argue space datacenters are essential as AI grows because terrestrial facilities strain power grids and water supplies, with SpaceX claiming its satellites would harness near-constant solar power at lower cost and reduced environmental impact. However, critics note that deployment technology is still being developed and remains far off; a July Government Accountability Office report acknowledged potential savings in land, electricity, and water but warned of engineering challenges such as inefficient cooling in space and risks from increased satellite collisions. The license requires SpaceX to begin deployment no later than November 2033 (d2), deploy 10% — or 100,000 satellites (q4) — by November 2035 (d5), and reach 50% by November 2038 (d7). It remains unclear whether SpaceX will place all 1 million satellites in orbit, where only about 17,000 currently exist. FCC chair Carr dismissed critics' doubts that the full constellation would be deployed or could take centuries to build, arguing competitors like Amazon should focus on their own constellations rather than question SpaceX's pace. Musk's space datacenter ambition was a key element in SpaceX's valuation when it went public in June, though OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argued Musk's optimism about deploying the satellites by 2027 (d12) was misleading.
items.title: FCC Approves SpaceX's Space Datacenter Satellite Plan

items.summary: The European Union said Wednesday that it 'strongly' rejected the premise behind new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States, and expected Washington to stick with a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US had unveiled these proposed tariffs covering 14 economies—including the EU and China—following a months-long probe into alleged excess production.
items.title: EU Rejects Premise of New US Tariffs

items.summary: In early Wednesday trading, US stocks linked to artificial intelligence fell sharply amid a broader sell-off. The tech-led Nasdaq plunged about 4 per cent (q1), while chip makers led the declines with Nvidia falling 8.7 per cent (q4) and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index losing 7.3 per cent (q5). Among other megacaps, Alphabet fell 5 per cent (q6), Amazon shed 5.4 per cent (q7), Microsoft dropped 3 per cent (q8), Apple was down 1.7 per cent (q9), and Anthropic slipped 2.1 per cent to close at US$81.90, below its US$83 IPO price (q10). The Nasdaq Composite fell about 4 per cent in early trading but later dropped 899.93 points, or 3.79 per cent, to 22,833.60; the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 602.93 points (1.21 per cent) to 49,415.77 and the S&P 500 fell 181.04 points (2.51 per cent) to 7,020.05. The Nasdaq Composite briefly fell about 20 per cent from its record closing high, flirting with bear market territory (q12). The rout came amid doubts over whether the debt-fuelled AI boom can deliver sufficient returns and fears of increased regulatory scrutiny following Democrats' midterm sweep; SWBC chief investment officer Chris Brigati said in a note that fundamental support for a year-end rally is not there because massive capex spending has yet to show evidence of delivering expected profits and revenue. The tech-heavy Nasdaq and S&P 500 remained on track for their worst November since 2008 (d3). Separately, Trump tariffs spooked Wall Street as the US proposed new excess-capacity levies on 14 major trading partners (q13), with China facing the highest rates at a proposed 20 per cent in addition to roughly 25 per cent duties from Trump's first term (q14, q15). Tariff concerns overshadowed economic data: the US economy grew faster than initially estimated in the third quarter while inflation rose further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 (d16). The S&P 500 technology sector led losses with a 5.2 per cent fall (q18), Dell Technologies fell 7 per cent despite raising its annual revenue and profit forecasts (q19), while rival PC maker HP gained 11.7 per cent after reporting fourth-quarter results above estimates (q20). Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.05-to-1 ratio on the NYSE (q21) and 2.97-to-1 on the Nasdaq (q22), with the S&P 500 posting eight new 52-week highs against 11 new lows and the Nasdaq Composite recording 17 new highs versus 424 new lows.
items.title: US Stocks Tumble as AI Rout and Trump Tariffs Rattle Markets

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nasdaq (early) 4 %; Dow Jones Industrial Average 11.7 %; S&P 500 (tech sector) 5.2 %.

items.summary: The US military described the controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic lead azide in Middletown, Iowa as a 'HUGE success,' with acting secretary Adam Telle stating mitigation efforts exceeded expectations and that EPA sensor readings had shown no values above 0.0. The Army declared the risk to residents 'as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible.' The explosives, stored for about 20 years, had degraded through recrystallisation, making them more prone to accidental detonation from friction or movement; lead azide is a highly volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own. Plans to detonate the material were paused multiple times following public outcry and legal challenges before Wednesday's blast, which residents reported feeling nothing from despite living as close as one mile (Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson) and eight miles away (Sandy Mabeus), with a farmer about 20 miles out hearing only a distant rumble. Officials noted no level of lead exposure is considered safe, though Middletown officials said early readings were promising; incoming Governor-elect Rob Sand called for more testing and immediate transparency, while FEMA administrator Cameron Hamilton announced additional resources and testing in the coming days and weeks.
items.title: US Army calls Iowa lead-explosives detonation a 'huge success' amid health fears

items.summary: A Jerusalem District Court judging panel has recommended that prosecutors drop or reconsider the majority of bribery and corruption charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially strengthening his position as caretaker prime minister. In Case 4,000 — which alleges a reciprocal arrangement between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder of Israel's largest telecoms company — Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara that 'the chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter.' The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's conduct in Case 2,000 met the threshold for criminality. In a third case, Case 1,000, which alleges he acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after receiving cigars and champagne, they left open the possibility of conviction but urged that 'in the public interest' there be a rethink about how the trial proceeds. Baharav-Miara said she would consider the recommendations. Netanyahu has consistently denied all allegations; in a televised statement he called for the trial to end immediately, describing it as ten years of suffering and incitement to hatred against him, his family, and his son. He was first charged in 2019, though proceedings have been prolonged partly by the recent Israel-Gaza war. The cases are known collectively as Case 4,000 (the telecoms arrangement), Case 2,000 (a quid-pro-quo with another media baron), and Case 1,000 (the Australian billionaire). Netanyahu's opponents argue his fear of prison has distorted his decision-making and increased his dependence on far-right coalition partners. The development comes as rival candidate Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form a government after an inconclusive election last month; although Netanyahu's bloc won more seats than Eisenkot's, neither achieved an outright majority.
items.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu

items.summary: On November 24, China announced the crew list for its Shenzhou-24 mission to the Tiangong space station. The roster includes the first-ever foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese crewed mission aboard the station. This milestone was reported by Taikobot as part of an article promoting China's 'Space for All' initiative.
items.title: China Names First Foreign Astronaut for Shenzhou-24 Mission

items.summary: The China Astronaut Research and Training Center reported that two Pakistani astronauts—Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud—who began training in China this spring have worked well together. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to visit the China Space Station. To support their training, the center developed a dedicated program for the Pakistani crew, produced bilingual Chinese-English manuals, and shifted from English-only instruction to bilingual teaching in both languages. In addition to basic Chinese classes, Shi Yusheng of the center said focused training was provided on frequently used terms and commands related to human spaceflight. Describing the effort, Shi told CGTN that "the astronauts worked very hard, working on their Chinese every day." The Pakistani crew also learned classical Chinese poetry as part of their program.
items.title: Pakistani Astronauts Train at China Space Station, Learning Chinese and Classical Poetry

items.summary: Yash Garg, an IIT Delhi graduate who shared his story on X, went from owing more than ₹1 crore in principal (with the total ballooning through credit-card interest) while in his second year—debt stemming from his father's real estate investments—to clearing it by June 2023. After ranking second in his department with a CGPA of 9.7 but failing Tower Research's final round, he took a ₹18 lakh-a-year job at Cohesity and moved to Bengaluru in July 2019 living on monthly expenses below ₹20,000; about a year later he found that almost his entire salary had gone toward interest while the principal stayed unchanged. Still owing ₹80 lakh when Google eventually hired him via a referral, Garg started an app business with his father and shifted to iOS games after Android apps struggled: buying a MacBook Pro for ₹2.1 lakh, porting their top Android game into Swift in six days, generating ₹6 lakh the first month and ₹24 lakh by the fourth month. Over the next 18 months the games crossed 200,000 downloads (mostly US users) and produced more than ₹2 crore in revenue; combined with his Google salary this cleared the debt before he resigned from Google just before turning 25 to pursue entrepreneurship full-time. His startup Super Workday now has more than 300 paying customers—mostly US-based—and is close to $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR). In January 2025 Garg raised a $400,000 investment from South Park Commons at a $5.7 million valuation for an AI executive assistant.
items.title: IIT Delhi alumnus cleared ₹1 crore family debt before 25, then quit Google to build startup

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's gold reserves fell 8.7 per cent, from about $97.4 billion a year earlier, to approximately $106 billion in September 2026 (q1, q2), driven by lower gold prices as the metal dipped about 8.5 per cent to roughly $12,957 an ounce in September from around $14,163 an ounce in April 2026 (q4, q5, q6). RBI attributed the decline to rising US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy. Gold reserves made up 14.4 per cent of total foreign exchange reserves in September, down from 16.7 per cent at the start of fiscal 2026 (q11, q13), while gold holdings had risen between 23 per cent and 47 per cent on a year-on-year basis during March to August 2026 (q15, q16). The overall foreign exchange reserve nonetheless grew 6.75 per cent to $737.79 billion in September, cushioned by Foreign Currency Assets that increased more than 10 per cent to about $608.3 billion; RBI said the fall did not distort reserves and that imports were still covered for roughly 9.8 months at end-June 2026.
items.title: RBI Gold Reserves Fell 8.7% to $106 Billion in September

items.summary: Pranjal Paul, a fifth-year Computer Science PhD student at IIIT-H's Robotics Research Center supervised by Prof. Madhava Krishna and co-advised by Prof. Arun Kumar Singh, has been selected as one of 148 fellows across 38 countries for the 2026 Google PhD Fellowship Program in Machine Learning and ML Foundations, supported by Google.org. He is among nine Indian institution fellows and the fifth IIIT-H researcher to receive the award since its inception in 2009. His research improves autonomous-system reliability by embedding driving rules into neural-network-based learning so vehicles can steer, accelerate, brake safely while following traffic rules; he notes that a system succeeding in 99.9% of individual scenarios has only about a 36.8% probability of completing 1,000 independent scenarios without failure.
items.title: IIIT Hyderabad's Pranjal Paul Selected for 2026 Google PhD Fellowship

items.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced on X that Google's Neon model set a new Day-1 usage record on the company's paid APIs, while daily Antigravity token usage rose 82% since Argon launched just six weeks ago. The figures were attributed to Pichai and confirmed across multiple passages (q1 [83:86]: 82%, q3 [63:66]: 82%, q4 [87:90]: 82%), all citing the same eight-week reference period following Argon's launch. Neon is identified as Gemini 4 Neon, an advanced AI model developed by Google DeepMind (q2 [43:49]:
items.title: Google Reports Record Neon API Usage and Antigravity Token Growth

items.summary: A warning issued by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) over security risks associated with WhatsApp Web and desktop applications, particularly on shared computers, has raised concerns among employees in Hyderabad. The advisory comes after fraudsters who gain access to an active WhatsApp session could read personal conversations and group chats, impersonate account holders, ask contacts for money, or circulate malicious links. Karthik Mitra, an IT employee, said the I4C's warning came as a shock to 12 lakh employees of IT and ITeS sectors in Hyderabad, who now have to be careful while organisations should come up with more secure devices for their employees. Rahul Hegde B.K., deputy commissioner of police (cybersecurity), said unattended WhatsApp Web sessions or those accessed through compromised computers could lead to the theft of sensitive personal, official and financial information, besides the leakage of confidential organisational and government information. He noted that while technological advancements enable seamless access across multiple devices, users are often inadequately informed about the associated security risks and preventive measures. The DCP advised users to avoid accessing WhatsApp Web on office, shared and public computers and manually log out after every session, as closing the browser would not necessarily terminate an active session. Users were also advised to regularly review linked devices, enable two-step verification and biometric security, avoid scanning unknown QR codes or sharing device-linking codes, independently verify unusual financial requests even those received from known contacts, keep computers, browsers and security software updated, and use private browsing mode on a trusted computer if usage is unavoidable. The DCP called upon educational institutions, IT professionals, government employees and private organisations to promote cybersecurity awareness and responsible digital practices, while encouraging technology companies to incorporate more prominent security warnings, periodic authentication, automatic session expiry options and user-friendly security alerts to minimise the risk of unauthorised access.
items.title: I4C Warning On WhatsApp Web Raises Security Concerns Among Hyderabad Employees

items.summary: The US Trade Representative has determined that India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are 'unreasonable' under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, proposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods (which could fall to 17 per cent if a qualifying trade agreement is reached). New Delhi has rejected the charge, stating it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. The USTR's case centers on India's flagship manufacturing initiatives—Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), the Production Linked Incentive scheme and IBEF—which Washington argues encourage production beyond what domestic demand justifies, potentially creating export surpluses that undercut American manufacturers. The report also cites inadequate labour protections, noting India's 28.6 per cent manufacturing GDP labour share in 2022 was about 19 percentage points below the US level; sustained market-access barriers favouring Indian producers; and reliance on imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies such as China. The investigation began in March 2026, covered 16 economies, and has produced determinations against 14 of them, including India.
items.title: US Proposes Tariffs on India Over Manufacturing Capacity Policies

items.summary: The United States Trade Representative proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods alongside 13 other nations, citing industrial excess capacity and foreign subsidies while exempting smartphones, generic medicines, and specific electronics ahead of the Prime Minister's planned visit to the G20 Summit in Miami. In response, India's Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector, and New Delhi is reviewing the US Trade Representative's Section 301 findings concerning alleged excess manufacturing capacity across several economies. Officials reaffirmed their commitment to a bilateral trade agreement with the United States through dialogue but flagged concerns that the ongoing probe could result in US trade actions affecting export-focused manufacturing and MSMEs.
items.title: India responds to US tariff threats amid Section 301 manufacturing probe

items.summary: The Indian government responded Wednesday to the United States Trade Representative's (USTR) determination proposing fresh tariffs on 14 economies, including India and China, over alleged excess manufacturing capacity. In a statement from its Ministry of Commerce and Industry, New Delhi said the notice was under examination while asserting that India had engaged constructively throughout an eight-month investigation conducted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The ministry stated that in response to the Notice of Initiation and subsequent proceedings,
items.title: India Rejects US Excess-Capacity Tariff Determination

items.summary: Several Muslim clerics who attended a Monday Waqf Day event in Srinagar, where the national song Vande Mataram was played in full, expressed regret and said they had prayed for repentance. In a statement on Wednesday, the clerics said they neither endorsed the song in their hearts nor through their words, and that if their participation hurt anyone's religious sentiments, they sincerely repented before Allah and asked him to accept it. The event was attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson Dr Darakhshan Andrabi, Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad, and other dignitaries. All six stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 1875 poem Vande Mataram were played in accordance with a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year that mandated the full version at state functions, official events, and legislature sessions. In August, the President cleared the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, which put Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem; the amendment did not alter the stanzas but made disrespect or disruption punishable. The poem was abridged in 1937 when the Congress Working Committee approved only its first two stanzas to respect religious diversity. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq-led Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU), an amalgam of religious organisations and institutions, said there was no legal obligation to play the song at an official function and criticised the waqf board for playing it at an event organised by an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments. The MMU stated that playing Vande Mataram conflicted with Islam's principle of Tawheed, or absolute oneness of Allah, describing any expression attributing divinity to the motherland as contrary to fundamental Islamic belief and impermissible for Muslims. It said it was considering legal advice and urged Muslims entrusted with religious responsibilities to uphold their beliefs without compromise.
items.title: Muslim Clerics Repent After Vande Mataram Played at J&K Waqf Event

items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir government dismissed allegations that the Border Roads Organisation was constructing near high-altitude Sheshnag Lake, which had been triggered by a viral video showing heavy machinery operating nearby. Forest minister Altaf Kaloo said the earthmover in the footage was working 200 to 300 feet away from the lake and at a higher elevation, adding that not even a grain of soil had entered the water body. Omar Abdullah addressed the controversy but noted he could not proceed further because security arrangements were not in place; as a protected person, police advised him against going ahead, so he returned to hold another detailed meeting with his department.
items.title: J&K Government Says Sheshnag Lake Is Safe After Viral Video of Heavy Machinery

items.summary: The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced proposed excess-capacity tariffs against 14 of the 16 economies it investigated for industrial policies that allegedly drive overproduction, with rates set net of existing Section 301 duties and accounting for certain Section 232 tariffs. India faces a rate capped at 17% if it reaches a reciprocal trade agreement addressing Washington's concerns, or up to 25% otherwise; the article notes India has rejected the charge as no sector shows overproduction. Vietnam would face the highest proposed rate at 35%, adjustable to 20% under an agreement, while China faces up to 20% on top of existing duties, and Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand could each face up to 18%. The European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland are set at 15%, with Singapore at up to 20%. These measures follow the Supreme Court's strike-down of IEEPA-based tariffs earlier this year and precede public hearings beginning January 25, 2027, after written comments close on January 5, 2027. The USTR said the proposed duties are not final pending consultation.
items.title: US Proposes Tariffs on India and 13 Other Economies Over Alleged Excess Manufacturing Capacity

items.summary: The Indian government said Wednesday it remains committed to working with the United States toward an early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement while rejecting Washington's allegation that India has structural excess manufacturing capacity. The remarks followed the US proposal on Wednesday of 25 per cent tariffs (q1) on imports from India, capped at 17 per cent (q2) if the two countries reach a deal — a rate GTRI said gives India only a one-percentage-point edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand's 18 per cent deal rate (q9–q11), or three points over Vietnam and China's 20 per cent deal rate (q12–q13). The proposal stems from USTR investigations into structural excess capacity across 16 economies (q3); India noted the Section 301 investigation notice covering 14 economies, including itself (q4, q5), which remains under examination. GTRI characterized Trump's tariffs as recreating a reciprocal-tariff regime engineered to pressure trading partners into one-sided deals rather than addressing genuine overproduction.
items.title: India Rejects US Excess Capacity Claim, Vows to Fast-Track Trade Deal Amid Proposed Tariffs

items.summary: India has rejected the United States' allegations that its manufacturing sector suffers from structural excess capacity, pushing back against a Section 301 investigation by the Trump administration's Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) that could result in additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods. In a statement issued Wednesday, India's Ministry of Commerce and Industry said it had taken note of USTR's determination and was examining the notice, while maintaining that no sector has excess capacity and urging resolution through ongoing negotiations for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA). The proposed duties could reach 25%, though the rate may be capped at 17% if India enters into a reciprocal trade agreement addressing Washington's concerns; these rates are not final and remain subject to public consultations and hearings. The USTR investigation covers manufacturing practices across 16 economies, including China, the European Union, Japan, Vietnam (up to 35%), Bangladesh/Cambodia/Indonesia/Malaysia/Thailand (up to 18%), plus EU/Japan/South Korea/Taiwan/Switzerland at 15%. The investigation follows the US Supreme Court's decision striking down Trump-era tariffs under IEEPA, after which Washington initiated Section 301 investigations of the Trade Act of 1974. Under USTR's determination, stakeholders have until January 5, 2027 to submit written comments, with hearings scheduled to begin on January 25.
items.title: India Rejects US Excess Capacity Allegations Amid Proposed Tariffs

items.summary: A BitDelta India study titled 'India's VDA Inflection Point: Mapping the Path from Curiosity to Conviction' found that 41 per cent of surveyed wealthy investors—family offices and ultra-high-net-worth individuals—have interacted with digital assets through active investments, past holdings, or exploratory research. The report also highlighted a knowledge gap: as many as 68 per cent of respondents described their familiarity with virtual digital assets as basic, indicating that interest has outpaced deep technical understanding. Regulatory ambiguity was identified as the primary obstacle to larger capital inflows, with 59 per cent of those surveyed flagging policy uncertainty as a major concern. Bharat Web3 Association Chairman Dilip Chenoy noted that family offices emphasize governance, risk management, and long-term value, adding that continued dialogue among investors, industry players, and policymakers will be key to building the sector's foundation.
items.title: BitDelta India study finds two in five wealthy investors have engaged with crypto amid regulatory caution
